title: Demon Magus & Infernalist in PoE 1.0 Full Launch - My Exilecon Playtest Thoughts

sections.title: Intro
points: Straight up start the video with :  The Demon Magus might be the coolest thing they have done with minions so far in PoE 2
I got hands-on with it at Exilecon etc.
prompts: What was your first reaction when you saw the Demon Magus in the keynote?
How much time did you actually get with the Infernalist at Exilecon? Did the playtest change your mind from your initial read?
deeper: The presenter called the Demon Magus one of the coolest new things in the Infernal Ascendancy.

sections.title: Ground rules - what I'm covering
points: This is my subjective take from Exilecon playtest - not a guide, not a tier list.
I'll be covering Demon Magus, Infernal Hounds, and also looking at some of the Covenant skills

sections.title: Demon Magus - what it is
points: Explain it - The Infernal Ascendancy's Demon Magus binds a Scourge Demon to your will after allocating it.
Other things etc. experience from playtest etc lil details
prompts: How did it feel in practice - clunky or smooth?
What spell setup did you try in your playtest?
Does it feel like a real minion or more like a totem that follows you?
deeper: The Acolyte of Chayula now summons a companion clone similar to the Demon Magus, which can use any Corsair skill you give it.

sections.title: Infernal Hounds & Covenant skills
points: Infernal Hounds now give you three of them.
They gain a command skill that makes them charge in and explode.
Example: Covenant of Gore sacrifices life to create a swarm of blowflies that wither your enemies.

sections.title: How it compares - Acolyte of Chayula
points: Acolyte of Chayula now also has the possibility to summon a companion clone similar to the Demon Magus.
That clone can use any Corsair skill you give it.
The old Darkness mechanic moved to a keystone on the main passive tree.
prompts: Does moving Darkness to a keystone make Acolyte more or less appealing to you?

sections.title: Final thoughts
points: My plan: Infernalist with Demon Magus on 1.0 launch - my rough plan and why waiting for patch notes is so important.
The customization of socketed spells is the big draw for me.
prompts: Any concerns about how it'll scale into endgame?

sections.title: Outro
points: Drop a comment for viewers: are you also going Infernalist on launch?
Thanks for watching - see you in 1.0.

Demon Magus.summary: The Demon Magus is a new Infernalist ascendancy skill in PoE 2 1.0: a persistent, reviving minion/companion meta gem that casts spells you socket into it, with the spell costs paid by you.
changes: New Infernalist ascendancy skill: Demon Magus, a persistent minion/companion meta gem
Summons a Reviving Demon Magus which casts socketed Spells
Cost of Spells cast by the minion are paid by you
Spells cast by the minion cost 50% less
Minion deals 15% more Damage per different socketed Skill
Quality grants Minions 0-20% more Maximum Life
Requires Level 90; gem level 20 (Max)
lines: Demon Magus | Minion / Companion, Persistent, Meta / Level: 20 (Max) / Requires: Level 90
Summon a Reviving Demon Magus which casts socketed Spells.
Cost of Spells cast by Minion are paid by you
Spells cast by Minion cost 50% less
Minion deals 15% more Damage per different socketed Skill
Place one or more Skill Gems into this Meta Gem's sockets in the Skills Panel. The socketed skills will be incorporated into the Meta Gem's effect.

Infernal Hounds.summary: Infernal Hounds received a major upgrade in PoE 2 1.0: you now get three of them, and they gain a Command skill (Instability) that makes a hound charge, leap, and explode for large Fire damage.
changes: You now get three Infernal Hounds (up from one)
Hounds gain a Command skill: Instability — command a hound to charge at a target, leap at it, and explode dealing large Fire damage
Tooltip now notes the hound can be Commanded to explode on a target
Command: Instability has a 1.00s cast time, deals 1632 to 2447 Fire damage, and has a 1.9 metre explosion radius (at level 20)
Skill tags now include Command in addition to Minion, Persistent, Fire
lines: Summon a Reviving Infernal Hound which Ignites enemies near it. Can be Commanded to explode on a target.
Activate to Command one of your Infernal Hounds to charge at a target, leap at it and explode, dealing a large amount of Fire damage.

Covenant skills.summary: Infernal Covenant is a new choice-based mechanic in PoE 2 1.0 where you make a deal with a Scourge demon lord, selecting one of three covenants that each grant a skill.
changes: New mechanic: make a deal with a Scourge demon lord, usually sacrificing something to empower something else
Select one of three options to allocate: Covenant of Beidat, Covenant of Ghorr, or Covenant of K'Tash
Each option grants a corresponding skill
lines: Infernal Covenant | Select one option to allocate

Acolyte of Chayula.summary: The Acolyte of Chayula has been totally reworked: Herald of Chayula now causes all your hits to add Decay to monsters, and killing a monster triggers an explosion based on the Decay it had. The old Darkness mechanic has been moved entirely into a keystone on the main passive tree, and the Acolyte can now also summon a companion, similar to Demon Magus. Its tooltip wasn't shown yet.
changes: Herald of Chayula now causes all your hits to add Decay to monsters
Killing a monster triggers an explosion based on the amount of Decay it had
The old Darkness mechanic has been completely moved into a keystone on the main passive tree
The Acolyte can now also summon a companion, similar to Demon Magus

Covenant of Gore.summary: Covenant of Ghorr is a new Covenant skill in PoE 2 1.0, one of three demon-lord covenants (with Beidat and K'Tash) that sacrifice something to empower something else; Ghorr drains life to spawn a swarm of withering bloatflies.
changes: New skill: Covenant of Ghorr, a Covenant skill dealing with a demon lord of the Scourge
Covenants are one of three options (Covenant of Beidat, Covenant of Ghorr, Covenant of K'Tash) allocated via Infernal Covenant
Sacrifices life (5% Life per Second while active) to create a Swarm of Withering Bloatflies every few seconds
Covenant buff grants 15% more Damage over Time and 1% maximum Life recovery on Kill to you and allies within it
Spawns a Swarm every 2 seconds; Swarm duration 6 seconds; Covenant duration 10 seconds; radius 4 metres; Limit 1 Covenant
Cooldown 15.00s, Cast Time 0.60s, Requires Level 90
Modifiers to Cooldown Recovery Rate also apply to Swarm Spawn frequency
Quality grants 0-20% more Area of Effect
